C1.worst_defect: The hero is clear ('Point of sale for Vendure… keeps selling when the connection drops'), but 'Before you start' opens with developer requirements (Node '^20.19 || >=22.12', Postgres, RXDB_PREMIUM licence token) ahead of the counter facts I care about ('desktop Chrome only', 'iPad not tested', 'no cash drawer opening'). There is no short 'what your staff get' summary near the top.

C2.worst_defect: Very honest overall. The one thing that reads as a hidden cost: refunds on my own store say the refund 'stays Pending until an administrator settles it with two Admin API calls', which is honest but only tells me I depend on my developer for every refund.
C2.where: home 'Live demo or your own store' table, 'Refund a sale at the till' row; Limitations refund bullet

C3.worst_defect: Quick start is complete, with a 'Check it worked' step, but every step is for my developer (npm, tsx migration, CORS_ORIGINS, tokenMethod). The staff-readiness checklist (open register with a float, scanner, take card on own terminal, close with Z report) lives only in the long At the till page, with no link from step 'Sign in and sell'.

C4.worst_defect: Troubleshooting mixes cashier guidance with server-admin material on the same page ('needs_admin' GraphQL, 'VENDUREPOS_WEB_ALLOW_LAN_HTTP', errorCode list), and for unknown errorCodes says 'the till has no retry or skip… Those closures and cash records do not reach your Vendure store from this till, so keep the printed Z reports'. Refund guidance repeats the jargon 'a query for the refund's ID, then the settleRefund mutation'. At the till is very long (9 phone slices).
C4.where: troubleshooting text and slices; limitations refund bullet; at-the-till.phone.01-09

C5.worst_defect: The cashier-sheet image sits in an oversized framed box with lots of empty padding, and the till screenshots disagree on clock format: the hero shows '11:10 PM' while the cashier sheet shows 'open since 22:06'.
C5.where: at-the-till.desktop.03 (cashier sheet); home hero vs at-the-till

C6.worst_defect: No overflow, and tables stack into cards, but the pages I'd read between customers are long scrolls: At the till runs to 9 phone slices with no jump list visible beyond the collapsed 'On this page' bar, so finding 'Close the day' mid-shift means a lot of scrolling.

C7.worst_defect: Minor: Lighthouse flags 53 KiB unused JavaScript and 14 KiB legacy JavaScript on home, and mobile LCP is 2.3 s; everything else (titles, JSON-LD, sitemap, llms.txt, 0 images without alt, A11y/BP/SEO 100) is in order.

overall_worst.defect: On my own store (plugin 0.3.0) staff cannot refund at the till, and the docs explain the workaround in developer language: the refund 'stays Pending until an administrator settles it with two Admin API calls: a query for the refund's ID, then the settleRefund mutation'. A shop owner reading this between customers has no plain answer to 'a customer wants their money back, what do my staff do right now?'
overall_worst.where: home 'Live demo or your own store' table, refund row; Limitations refund bullet; At the till 'Refund' section
overall_worst.fix: Add a plain three-line 'When a customer wants a refund' box on At the till and the home table: give cash back with a Pay out quoting the order code, then tell whoever runs your store to settle it. Move the Admin API and settleRefund detail to Plugin setup only and link to it from there.
